business-api-context · Bunkai TMS

Business API map

Updated 2026-11-17 from upex-bunkai-tms origin/staging 4ccd8ede (sections first built 2026-10-12 from 98ee1b4): route handlers, lib/api/, the generated contract public/openapi.json (identical to what the openapi MCP serves) and the data and E2E maps of 2026-11-17. No live API call was made: every status code here is read from code. Every fact a figure shows is also in the text.

Overview

What the API lets the business do. Bunkai's API is the same surface the web app uses, so anything a QA team does in the browser can also be done by a script, a CI pipeline or an AI agent: sign in, build a project's module tree and user stories (or pull them from Jira), author ATCs (Acceptance Test Cases) anchored to acceptance criteria, chain them into Tests, start and record Runs, file and triage bugs with screenshot evidence, plan and close testing, compare a Run with the previous one, chat with the team, and read coverage, traceability and run reports. A test team can therefore run its whole loop headlessly and still produce the same evidence trail a person would.

Who may do what is decided in two places. The API gateway decides how a caller may arrive (public, browser session only, any signed-in caller, or a token carrying the right scope); the database decides what that person may touch (their workspace role: viewer, member, admin, owner, enforced by Row Level Security and the business functions). A token never has more power than the person who issued it; it can only have less. A handful of owner actions (delete or restore a workspace, export its data, issue or revoke tokens) are deliberately reserved for a person in a browser.

Money and irreversible actions sit behind the owner (billing details, payment method and retry of a failed renewal are owner-only too): the Cloud upgrade goes through Stripe and only takes effect when Stripe confirms payment, and deleting a workspace ends access for everyone immediately with a 30-day window to restore. Four things run without a person: a daily email digest and a daily storage cleanup, both triggered by Vercel Cron, the Stripe webhook, and background workers that do Jira imports, data exports and deletion emails after the request has answered.

Since the first version of this map the same surface also covers team chat, saved filter views, archive and restore of structure, ATCs and milestones, bulk edits, image evidence on run steps and defects, one-call submission of automated Run results, closing a test plan with a verdict, billing maintenance (company details, invoices, payment method, retry of a failed renewal), a per-workspace Jira connection with per-project defect-sync settings, removal of a teammate, and an application-level throttle on the sign-in family.

Permission and auth model

Every handler under app/api/ is wrapped by withApiHandler (lib/api/handler.ts) and must declare one of four postures; there is no default, so a route without one does not compile. A source scan (lib/api/route-posture-scan.ts) diffs every handler against the committed snapshot lib/api/route-capability-coverage.snapshot.json. The committed snapshot at origin/staging 4ccd8ede lists 160 handlers (158 under app/api/, 2 under app/auth/), up from 107 on 2026-10-12; the scan itself was not re-run (the product repo is read-only here), so the counts below are read from the snapshot file. The middleware (middleware.ts) only refreshes the session cookie on /api/*; it never blocks an API request.

Schemes

Four credential schemes coexist (plus the throttle in auth-rate-limits), each with its own section: the browser cookie session (auth-cookie-session), the personal access token (auth-pat), and two system secrets (auth-system-callers: the cron secret for the two cron routes, the Stripe signature). The OpenAPI contract declares them as cookieAuth (cookie sb-{project-ref}-auth-token), bearerAuth and cronAuth; the Stripe signature is not in the contract.

Precedence and refusals

  • A request carrying Authorization: Bearer … is always treated as a PAT, even when a session cookie is also present (bearer first, resolveIdentity).
  • No credential on a non-public route: 401 unauthorized "Authentication required."
  • Any PAT failure (wrong shape, unknown prefix, hash mismatch, revoked, expired): one uniform 401 unauthorized "Invalid token." The caller cannot tell which check failed.
  • Missing scope: 403 forbidden with details.reason = missing_capability and details.required_capability, so a client can tell it from a role refusal, which is also 403.
  • A PAT on a cookie-only route: 403 forbidden with the route's reason (for example "Personal access tokens cannot issue tokens. Use a browser session.").
  • Too many sign-in, code-confirm or check-email attempts: 429 rate_limited with a Retry-After header and details.retry_after_seconds (auth-rate-limits).
  • Role refusals come from Postgres: a write by a viewer surfaces as 403 forbidden (details.reason = not_a_member); a resource in a workspace the caller cannot see answers 404, the same as a missing one.

Scheme: browser cookie session

The browser scheme. A person proves who they are to Supabase Auth and receives the Supabase session cookie (sb-*); the API reads it on every call.

  1. Magic link: POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link asks Supabase Auth to email a link (only to an existing account; shouldCreateUser is false). The answer is always { ok: true }, also for an unknown address (anti-enumeration); a Supabase rate limit surfaces as 429 rate_limited. An audit row is written best-effort.
  2. The emailed link lands on GET /auth/callback, which verifies the token hash statelessly (so a link requested on a laptop works on a phone) and sets the session cookie, then redirects to next (a same-origin path only, checked on the parsed URL; default /projects). The magic-link request validates next with the same rule up front, so a crafted value is refused (422) instead of being mailed in the link. Failures redirect to /login?error=magic_link_invalid.
  3. OAuth (GitHub, Google): GET /auth/oauth/{provider} sets a state cookie and redirects to the provider; the callback rejects a state mismatch with 403 OAUTH_STATE_MISMATCH before exchanging the code.
  4. Headless password sign-in and email-code confirmation (auth-pat) also set the cookie on the response, so a script can hold a browser-grade session.
  5. Every later /api/v1 call: the gateway calls Supabase getUser; the principal holds all four scopes and the handler queries Postgres with the user's own session, so RLS filters the rows.
  6. Refresh: the middleware calls getUser on every matched request and writes refreshed cookies back; there is no separate refresh endpoint.
  7. Page routes: the middleware redirects a signed-out visit to /login for /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity, /atcs and /workspaces pages, except the public workspace-restore landing page reached from the deletion email.
  8. The active workspace is a separate preference cookie (bk_active_ws) set by POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace (cookie-only, 403 "You are not a member of that workspace." for a foreign id).

Scheme: personal access token (PAT)

The programmatic scheme for CLIs, CI and AI agents. A PAT acts as the person who issued it, narrowed by its scopes; the token string is bk_pat_{12-char prefix}.{secret} and is shown exactly once.

How to obtain one

PathCredential neededScopesWorkspace bindingExpiry
POST /api/v1/auth/signin (email + password)none (public)default atc:read, atc:write, run:execute; workspace:admin refused (403, checked before the password is verified, so a refused request has no side effect)none (global token)never, unless pat_expires_in_days (1 to 365)
POST /api/v1/auth/signup then POST /api/v1/auth/confirm (6 to 8 digit email code)none (public)same as sign-innonesame as sign-in
POST /api/v1/tokensbrowser session onlyany non-empty subset of the fouroptional workspace_id; mandatory for workspace:admin, which also needs admin or owner role therenever, unless expires_in_days (1 to 365)

Sign-in and code confirmation are throttled per network source and per account (429 rate_limited, see auth-rate-limits). Sign-up answers 202 pending_confirmation and issues nothing; the token and session come only from /auth/confirm. Sign-in and confirm return the Supabase session tokens next to the PAT, but those session tokens are not accepted as a bearer on /api/v1: the bearer branch only accepts the bk_pat_ family and answers 401 otherwise.

On every call

  1. The gateway reads the bearer, looks the token up by prefix with the service-role client and compares the SHA-256 of the secret against the separate secret table.
  2. A revoked or expired token gets the same 401 as a forged one. last_used_at is updated fire-and-forget.
  3. The route scope is checked (403 missing_capability); for the 16 workspace:admin handlers the token must also be bound to the target workspace (403 "This token is not scoped to a workspace…" or "…scoped to a different workspace.").
  4. The API mints a 60-second user JWT (signed with the Supabase JWT secret, never returned) so Postgres RLS sees the token owner exactly as for a browser call. Scopes are not in that JWT: Postgres enforces the role, the API enforces the scope.

Submitting automated Runs

POST /api/v1/runs/submissions accepts a bearer token only: a cookie session gets 403 token_required, and a token with no workspace binding gets 403 token_not_workspace_scoped. The token name is recorded as the executor. See group-automated-runs.

End of life

Revocation (DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id}, browser only) stamps revoked_at; rows are never deleted. Leaving a workspace or deleting it revokes the tokens bound to it, and a pipeline using one starts getting 401. Removing a teammate (DELETE /workspaces/{id}/members/{userId}) revokes that person's tokens bound to the workspace in the same transaction. A PAT can never issue or revoke a PAT. GET /api/v1/tokens (any credential) lists the caller's own tokens without secrets.

Scheme: system callers (cron secret, Stripe signature)

Three routes are called by systems, not people, and hold no PAT: two Vercel Cron routes that share one secret, and Stripe. All declare the public posture and authenticate inside the handler.

CallerRouteCredentialRefusalWhat it changes
Vercel Cron, daily 08:00 UTC (registered from the production deployment only, vercel.json)GET /api/v1/admin/send-digest (cron); POST is the manual retryAuthorization: Bearer {CRON_SECRET} (cronAuth in the contract)401 unauthorized "Invalid or missing CRON_SECRET."claims one digest row per user and UTC day, sends one Resend email per user, returns a run summary
Vercel Cron, daily 03:00 UTC (production deployment only, vercel.json)GET /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup (cron); POST is the manual retry and the only way to run it on stagingAuthorization: Bearer {CRON_SECRET}401 unauthorized "Invalid or missing CRON_SECRET."; 500 when the queue cannot be readexpires evidence uploads never committed or claimed, deletes the Storage objects queued by removals and deletions, purges finished queue rows after 7 days; returns counts
StripePOST /api/v1/billing/webhook (not in the OpenAPI contract)stripe-signature header verified against the webhook secret400 bad_request when missing or invalidapplies checkout events to the checkout session and, when paid, upgrades the workspace plan; applies invoice events (invoice.payment_failed, invoice.paid) to the failed-renewal grace window; records the new card summary of a payment-method setup session

Webhook outcomes: an event type outside the four checkout events, the two invoice events and the setup-mode completion answers 200 ignored; a setup-mode session (a payment-method replacement, never a purchase) never reaches the checkout rule; an invoice event for a customer the database does not know yet answers 502 only while the event is less than an hour old, then 200; a checkout session the database does not know yet answers 502 upstream_error so Stripe redelivers; a database failure answers 500. Duplicate events are deduplicated by event id inside bunkai_apply_billing_checkout_webhook_event (and the invoice RPC for invoice events).

Scheme: application-level throttle on the sign-in family

The app now counts attempts itself instead of relying on Supabase Auth alone. It protects the three calls where a guess is cheap: whether an email has an account, a password, and an emailed code. The counter lives in Postgres (a sliding window per key, atomic under an advisory lock) and the store only ever sees a keyed digest of the caller's network address or of the lower-cased email, never the raw value.

CallBudget per network sourceBudget per accountWhen it is checked
POST /auth/check-email10 per 60 seconds, 60 per hournonebefore the body is parsed and before the directory is consulted, so the refusal is identical for every address and malformed submissions spend budget too
POST /auth/signin10 per 60 seconds, 60 per hour10 per 15 minutessource first (before the body is parsed), then the account once the email is known, before Supabase is called
POST /auth/confirm10 per 60 seconds, 60 per hour10 per 15 minutessame order as sign-in
  • Refusal: 429 rate_limited, a fixed message ("Too many attempts. Please wait and try again."), details.retry_after_seconds and a Retry-After header. The text is identical for every caller. When Supabase itself throttles the code check, the same shape is used with a 60-second hint.
  • The network source is read only from headers Vercel itself asserts (x-vercel-forwarded-for, then x-real-ip); a plain x-forwarded-for is not trusted. Without either header every request shares one unknown bucket.
  • Fail closed: if the counter store cannot answer, the call is refused with 502 upstream_error instead of skipping the budget.
  • Expired counter rows are swept hourly by pg_cron (bunkai-sweep-rate-limit-hits).
  • Not throttled by this layer: POST /auth/signup, /auth/resend and /auth/magic-link; those still depend on Supabase's own limits (429 rate_limited).

Data: automatic-processes (rate-limit sweep). Features: feature-access (FEAT-001, FEAT-002).

Scope design worth knowing: there is no bug scope and no report scope. Filing, assigning, correcting and advancing bugs need atc:write; every report and list needs atc:read; only the run-state writes need run:execute (start, mark, finish, abort, the three evidence writes on a step, and run submission: 8 handlers). Chat needs no scope at all. A token with run:execute alone can start and close Runs but cannot read the Test it runs (GET /tests/{id} needs atc:read).

The 119 contract paths match 119 route files under app/api/; the code also holds two route files outside the contract (GET /api/openapi and POST /api/v1/billing/webhook). 160 handlers in the posture snapshot = 155 contract operations + the Stripe webhook + 4 bypass handlers.

Group: sign-up and sign-in

Who calls it: the login page (email-first form) and headless clients. Why: get an account and a credential. What it changes: Supabase Auth users and sessions; a PAT row on confirm and sign-in; a magic-link audit row.

OperationBusiness meaningNotable answers
POST /auth/check-emailRoute an entered email to password, code entry or sign-up200 { exists, confirmed }: deliberately reveals whether an account exists; 429 rate_limited past 10 a minute or 60 an hour per source
POST /auth/signupCreate an unconfirmed account and email a code202 pending_confirmation (also for the loser of two concurrent sign-ups for one fresh address); 409 existing account; 422 password over 72 bytes, email over 253 characters or on a reserved domain (example.com, .test and similar, which can never receive the code); 429 Supabase rate limit
POST /auth/confirmProve the email with the code; get session + PAT200; 401 invalid or expired code; 403 if workspace:admin requested (checked before the code is consumed); 429 throttled; 502 upstream
POST /auth/resendSend the code again202 sent; 429
POST /auth/signinPassword sign-in; get session + PAT200; 401 "Invalid email or password." (uniform); 403 if workspace:admin requested (checked before the password); 429 throttled; 502 upstream
POST /auth/magic-linkEmail a sign-in link to an existing accountalways 200 { ok: true } except 429 and 502

Passwords are 8 characters to 72 bytes at sign-up (bytes, not characters: accents and symbols take 2 to 4 bytes; a longer one is 422 too_big) and 6 to 128 characters at sign-in. Throttling: auth-rate-limits. Data: flow-sign-in-and-onboarding. Features: feature-access (FEAT-001, FEAT-002). Journey: journey-sign-in-and-onboarding.

Group: identity and tokens

Who calls it: the app shell (who am I, which workspace is active), Settings, Tokens, and automation clients checking who they are. What it changes: the active-workspace cookie and access_tokens.

  • GET /me (any credential): the principal, how it authenticated, its workspaces and an effective workspace (the token's binding, else the first visible one).
  • POST /me/active-workspace (cookie only): set the browser's active workspace; a PAT passes workspace_id on each request instead (for example POST /tests answers 422 "workspace_id is required for token-authenticated calls.").
  • GET /tokens (any credential), POST /tokens and DELETE /tokens/{id} (cookie only): list, issue (201, secret shown once) and revoke PATs. Details in auth-pat.

Data: entity-access-token, state-access-token. Features: FEAT-003 (feature-access), FEAT-005 (feature-workspace).

The tenant itself: create it, rename it, leave it, take the data out, delete it and bring it back. Highest blast radius in the API: one call can end access for a whole team.

PATCH /workspaces/{id}workspace:admin + bound tokenowner (RLS); others get 403workspace name only

Group: team members

Who calls it: an admin or owner removing a teammate from the Members list. DELETE /workspaces/{id}/members/{userId} needs workspace:admin (a PAT must be bound to this workspace) and a live admin or owner role. Re-inviting is the only way back.

What one call changes, all or nothing: the membership row is deleted, the person's tokens bound to this workspace are revoked, pending invites addressed to their email are revoked, every defect assigned to them becomes unassigned, and a member.removed activity event is written. Authorship (what they filed, ran or wrote) stays.

  • Rank ladder: viewer < member < admin < owner. A caller may remove a target whose role does not outrank theirs (an admin can remove admins, members and viewers; only an owner can remove an owner), never themselves.
  • Order of refusals: workspace not visible, deleted or target not a member: 404 (the same body for both); caller is a member or viewer: 403 not_a_member; target is the caller: 409 cannot_remove_self with details.leave_endpoint (use DELETE /workspaces/{id}/membership); an admin targeting an owner: 403 cannot_remove_owner; backstop when the workspace would be left with no owner: 409 sole_owner.
  • Success: 200 with the removal summary.

Data: flow-invite-and-membership, entity-workspace, entity-access-token. Features: FEAT-042 (feature-workspace). Journey (e2e map): journey-remove-member.

Group: team invites

Who calls it: an admin or owner growing the team, and the invitee redeeming the link. Bunkai sends no invite email: the issue call returns the accept URL once and the inviter shares it.

  • Issue, list, rotate, revoke (POST|GET /workspaces/{id}/invites, POST|DELETE …/invites/{inviteId}): workspace:admin, token bound to that workspace, admin or owner (RLS). Roles offered: viewer, member, admin; never owner. Inviting an existing active member is refused.
  • Accept (POST /invites/accept): any authenticated caller, because the invitee is not a member yet. Full answer table in journey-invite-and-join. A new refusal: 409 inviter_not_authorized when the inviter was removed, demoted below the invited role or deleted since issuing the invite. The membership write and the invite stamp are now one database call.
  • Seats are not checked when inviting or accepting (data map flow-invite-and-membership).

Data: entity-invite, state-invite. Features: FEAT-006 (feature-workspace).

Group: billing and plan

The only place money changes hands. Who calls it: the billing settings pages, and Stripe.

  • GET /workspaces/{id}/billing (atc:read): plan (the effective one) and stored_plan, purchased and active seats, project count, oldest run age, grace_ends_at and a billing block (can_edit, company profile, card brand and last four, payment state, subscription state, grace window, retry_available; null for a workspace that does not pay through Stripe); admins and owners only, others get 404.
  • POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout (workspace:admin, bound token, Idempotency-Key required, owner only): returns the Stripe hosted checkout URL. 422 plan_not_upgradable on Cloud or Enterprise, 422 seat_quantity_invalid, 409 checkout_in_progress, 503 payment_processor_unavailable. A workspace with an unpaid renewal is refused with 422 plan_not_upgradable (details.reason = payment_overdue): the way back is the payment method and the retry (group-billing-maintenance).
  • POST …/billing/checkout/cancel (same gate): expire the open session after Stripe's cancel page.
  • Stripe webhook: see auth-system-callers. Plan limits: only the project limit is enforced (422 project_limit_reached on project creation, judged against the effective plan, so a Cloud workspace past its grace window is held to the Community limit; the 422 details name the plan, limit, usage and the owners to ask).

Data: flow-billing-upgrade, state-checkout-session, integration-stripe. Features: FEAT-007 (feature-workspace).

Group: billing maintenance

After the upgrade, the owner keeps the subscription healthy: company details for invoices, the invoices themselves, the card, and recovery from a failed renewal. Who calls it: the Billing settings page. All five calls are for a workspace that pays through Stripe; for a workspace without a paid subscription they answer 404 (reads) or 409 no_active_subscription (writes).

OperationCredential and roleWhat it doesNotable answers
PATCH /workspaces/{id}/billing/detailsworkspace:admin + bound token; owner only (checked before the body is read)pushes company name, billing email and address to the Stripe customer first, then stores them; later invoices carry them, issued ones never change403 not_workspace_owner; 409 no_active_subscription; 422 field rules; 502 upstream_error (nothing stored); 503 processor not configured
GET …/billing/invoicesatc:read; owner and adminnewest-first page of issued invoices read live from Stripe (no local copy; drafts and voided ones not listed)404 for any caller who may not read billing; 400 bad limit or starting_after
GET …/billing/invoices/{invoiceId}/pdfatc:read; owner and adminthe route proxies the PDF (never a redirect to Stripe)404 for an unknown invoice or one of another workspace (same answer); 409 invoice_pdf_unavailable with details.retryable
POST …/billing/payment-methodworkspace:admin + bound token; owner only; Idempotency-Key requiredreturns a Stripe-hosted setup page (card only); the webhook records brand, last four and expiry and makes it the default409 no_active_subscription; 502 (retry with a NEW key)
POST …/billing/retryworkspace:admin + bound token; owner only; Idempotency-Key requiredpays the invoice that opened the grace window with the default method200 only when Stripe says paid; 402 payment_declined (card_declined or requires_action); 409 retry_not_available (reasons no_failed_renewal, payment_method_not_replaced, retry_in_progress, invoice_not_payable); 502 when the payment could not be confirmed
  • Failed renewal: Stripe's invoice.payment_failed on a renewal opens a 14-day grace window from the first failure; paid limits hold strictly before its end and the workspace reads as Community from that instant (the stored plan stays Cloud, nothing is deleted).
  • Retry is offered only after a replacement payment method was confirmed after the failure. Three guards stop a double charge: the Idempotency-Key, an atomic claim (a claim older than 5 minutes is treated as abandoned) and Stripe's own idempotency key per attempt. A decline, a required card action or a timeout leaves the failed state, the grace date and the retry path exactly as they were; a charge that timed out but went through is reconciled by the invoice.paid webhook.

Data: flow-billing-maintenance, entity-billing-state, state-billing-payment, integration-stripe. Features: FEAT-043 (feature-workspace). Journey (e2e map): journey-manage-billing.

Group: project structure

Describes the product under test: projects, a module tree, user stories and their ordered acceptance criteria. Who calls it: members in the project explorer and automation that seeds structure. What it changes: projects, modules, user_stories, acceptance_criteria.

  • Every DELETE here archives (soft delete), never removes rows: module subtree, user story (with its criteria and ATCs, one timestamp), criterion. Archiving the last active criterion drops the story back to draft. Bringing a module subtree back is group-archive-restore.
  • Listings of modules, user stories and criteria show live rows only; ?include_archived=true (and nothing else) adds archived ones. GET /projects/{id}/modules returns the whole tree in one call (modules, stories, criteria as flat lists; with the flag, archived_atcs too).
  • Creating a project (POST /workspaces/{id}/projects) and a user story (POST /modules/{id}/user-stories) requires an Idempotency-Key (400 without).
  • Story status ready_to_test requires at least one active criterion.
  • Module rename and move are validated by the database (sibling slug clash, cycles, depth above 6).
  • GET /workspaces/{id}/projects (atc:read) lists a workspace's projects, optionally by exact ?slug= (the Bunkai CLI resolves --project this way); a foreign, nonexistent or deleted workspace answers the same empty 200 as an empty one, a failing read answers 500, never an empty list. There is still no single-project read; Home uses GET /workspaces/{id}/recent-projects (group-insights).

Data: entity-module, entity-user-story, state-user-story, flow-author-structure. Features: FEAT-010, FEAT-011, FEAT-012 (feature-authoring).

Group: Jira import

Pulls user stories and criteria from Jira by JQL, one way. POST /imports (atc:write, member) answers 202 with a job id; GET /imports/{id} (atc:read) is polled until completed or failed. One active import per project (409). The workspace must have its own Jira connection first: without one POST /imports answers 409 jira_not_connected and creates no job (group-jira-connection). Traced in journey-jira-import.

Data: flow-jira-import, state-async-job, integration-jira. Features: FEAT-013 (feature-authoring).

Group: Jira connection and defect-sync settings

Two layers. The workspace owns one Jira connection (site URL, account email, API token) that the Jira import uses. Each project then says where its defects would go (a Jira project key, an issue type, on or off). Who calls it: owners and admins in Settings, and any member who needs to see whether Jira is connected.

OperationCredential and roleWhat it doesNotable answers
GET /workspaces/{id}/jira-connectionatc:read; any active membermembers see only { connected }; owners and admins also see site URL, email, has_token, updated_at, updated_by. The token is never returned404 for a workspace the caller cannot see; 403 for a token bound to another workspace
PUT …/jira-connectionworkspace:admin + bound token; live admin or ownersaves the connection; the token is write-only, stored encrypted in Supabase Vault, required on the first save and whenever the site URL changes. Saving does not call Jira403 admin_required; 422 reasons invalid_site_url, invalid_email, token_required, invalid_body
DELETE …/jira-connectionsameremoves the connection and the stored token; imports stop working until it is connected again204; 404 not_connected
POST …/jira-connection/checksameone read-only call to Jira (/myself, 5-second budget, no retry, redirects refused); no body tests the stored connection, all three fields test unsaved values200 with ok: false and a reason kind is not an HTTP error; 422 incomplete_body; 429 check_in_progress (one check at a time per person)
GET /projects/{id}/tracker-settingsatc:read; any member or viewerdestination key, issue type, on or off; a never-configured project answers sync off, no key, issue type "Bug"404 for a project the caller cannot see
PUT …/tracker-settingsworkspace:admin + bound token; live admin or ownersaves the settings. Switching on runs the connection check first and saves nothing when it fails422 connection_check_failed (with details.check), invalid_destination_key (2 to 10 capitals, digits or underscores), invalid_issue_type; 409 queue_confirmation_required or queue_count_mismatch when the save would queue unsent defects until confirm_queue_count equals queue_count; 429 check_in_progress
POST …/tracker-settings/checksamechecks the destination key and issue type against Jira with the workspace connection200 ok: false with a reason; 422 malformed key or issue type (no request sent to Jira); 429
  • Every change to the connection is audited (jira_connection.connected, .changed, .disconnected); the audit payload carries the site host only, never the email or a secret.
  • The site URL must be an Atlassian Cloud address of the form https://{name}.atlassian.net; nothing else is contacted. The token should be a classic (unscoped) Atlassian API token.
  • Today these calls only configure. The data map found no worker that creates Jira issues from defects, so enabling the sync queues defects as pending but nothing leaves Bunkai (see discovery-gaps).

Data: entity-jira-connection, flow-jira-connection-and-tracker, integration-jira. Features: FEAT-040, FEAT-041 (feature-jira-sync). Journey (e2e map): journey-connect-jira.

Group: ATC authoring and library

The core asset of the product. Writes (atc:write, member): create (201, Idempotency-Key required), edit with the expected version (full replace of steps, assertions and criteria bindings), duplicate, bulk edit. Reads (atc:read): one ATC by id, which Tests use an ATC, full-text search by title and tags, whole-library CSV export. Archive and restore are in group-archive-restore.

  • Anchoring is enforced on every write: criteria must belong to the story (422 ac_outside_user_story), the module must be in the story's project subtree (422 module_outside_project_subtree).
  • Optimistic lock: a stale version answers 409 conflict with details.reason = version_conflict and details.current_version. An edit reports how many Tests are affected, because Tests hold references, not copies.
  • At most 10 tags; title at least 3 characters; slug collision 409 slug_collision (retryable).
  • GET /atcs/{id} is lean by default (header fields only); ?expand= takes a comma-separated list of steps, assertions, acceptance_criteria, used_in (400 names an unrecognised value). A missing, archived or inaccessible ATC is the same 404; responses are Cache-Control: private, no-store.
  • POST /atcs/bulk-edit changes ONE field (tags add or remove, module, layer, priority) on 1 to 200 ATCs of one project. Partial success is the normal shape: one outcome per ATC, a refused ATC never rolls back the others, an ATC already holding the value is unchanged (no version bump, no event), a per-item version refuses a stale ATC (stale_version), and dry_run: true writes nothing. 422 when the selection is empty, above 200 or has an unknown field; status is not editable (it is set by Runs). Each changed ATC emits its own atc.updated event.
  • An archived ATC is frozen: edit and duplicate answer 409 atc_archived. There is still no hard delete of an ATC.

Data: entity-atc, flow-author-atc. Features: FEAT-014, FEAT-015 (feature-authoring). Journey: journey-author-atc.

Group: archive and restore

Nothing in the product is hard-deleted by a member: archiving hides, restoring brings back, and archived rows stay as evidence in past Runs, traceability and defects. Who calls it: members in the module tree, the ATC library and the milestone list. All five calls need atc:write and the member role (a viewer gets 403, a non-member 404).

OperationWhat it doesRules a client hits
DELETE /modules/{id} (in group-structure)archives the module, its descendants, their stories, criteria and ATCs with one timestamp and one batch idlistings hide it until ?include_archived=true
POST /modules/{id}/restorebrings back exactly what that archive took (descendant modules, stories, criteria, ATCs); all or nothing; module.restored event per change200 changed: false for an active module; 409 with details.reason ancestor_archived, depth_exceeded, name_collision, story_key_collision or concurrent_change; rows archived on their own earlier stay archived
DELETE /atcs/{id}archives one ATC: it leaves lists, search, the command palette and the Test chain picker; no Test chain is edited204; archiving an archived ATC is the same 204 with no new event
POST /atcs/{id}/restoreclears the ATC's own archive200 changed: false for a live ATC or one whose only archive is its parent's; a restore never restores a parent; an ATC under an archived module or story comes back with that parent
POST /milestones/{id}/archivehides the milestone and makes it read-only; its name stays reserved; its plans, tests and Runs are untouched200 changed: false when already archived; edit, attach and detach answer 409 milestone_archived; a new milestone with the same name answers 409 milestone_name_archived
POST /milestones/{id}/restoreputs it back as it was (past target date kept, never re-validated)200 changed: false for an active milestone
  • User stories have no restore endpoint: a story archived with its module comes back through that module's restore.
  • ?include_archived=true applies to the module, user story, criterion and milestone listings only; each archived row carries its archive data.
  • Test and traceability reads mark archived ATCs (atcs[].archived_at) instead of hiding them.

Data: flow-archive-and-restore. Features: FEAT-047 (feature-authoring). Journey (e2e map): journey-archive-and-restore.

Group: test design

Turns ATCs into executable scenarios and plans: Tests (ordered chains of ATC references), test plans, milestones and the environments a Run must name.

AreaWrites (atc:write)Rules a client hits
Testscreate (Idempotency-Key required, PAT must pass workspace_id), reorder, replace tags; reads: GET /tests?tag= returns one newest-first page (limit default 20, max 50, next_cursor null when no more remain), GET /tests/{id} marks archived ATCs in the chain422 chain_empty; 404 when a chained ATC is outside the workspace; reorder must keep the same ATCs (422 chain_mismatch / chain_invalid) and the current version (409)
Test planscreate, edit, add Tests (Idempotency-Key required), remove a Testa Test whose chain leaves the plan's project: 422 test_outside_plan_project; closed plan: 409; listing accepts ?status=open|closed (400 otherwise); plan rows carry verdict, summary, closed_by, closed_at; closing and reopening a plan is group-plan-lifecycle
Milestonescreate, editname unique per project (an archived milestone keeps its name reserved: 409 milestone_name_archived); date within 5 years; the list hides archived milestones unless ?include_archived=true; archive, restore and attaching plans are in group-archive-restore and group-plan-lifecycle
Environmentscreate, rename, deletedelete refused with 409 while Runs reference it; a new project has none, so no Run can start

Data: entity-test, flow-compose-test-and-plan, flow-environments, state-test-plan. Features: FEAT-016 to FEAT-019 (feature-test-design).

Group: close a test plan, attach plans to milestones

Closes the loop on planning. A plan is closed with a verdict when its testing is done, and milestones group plans so readiness can be read per release. Who calls it: leads and members on the plan and milestone pages. All four calls need atc:write.

OperationWhoWhat it doesNotable answers
POST /test-plans/{id}/closethe plan's creator (while they still hold write access), admins and owners; re-checked on every callcloses an open plan with a required verdict (passed or failed) and an optional summary (up to 4,000 characters); writes verdict, closer, time and a frozen copy of the plan's progress together; the plan becomes read-only403 close_forbidden for a plain member who did not create it and for a viewer; 409 test_plan_not_open (also the loser of two simultaneous closes); 422 verdict_required or verdict_invalid or summary too long; 404 non-disclosing
POST /test-plans/{id}/reopensame rulereturns a closed plan to open and clears verdict, summary, closer, time and the progress snapshot; the close and reopen entries stay in the history409 when the plan is already open
POST /projects/{id}/milestones/{milestoneId}/plansmember or aboveattaches one or more plans to a milestone; a plan may serve several milestones. Idempotency-Key required201; 409 milestone_plan_exists (the WHOLE selection is rejected when one plan is already attached), milestone_archived; 422 plan_outside_project (a plan of another project, another workspace or unknown: one uniform answer), milestone_plan_limit (at most 50 plans), empty selection
DELETE …/milestones/{milestoneId}/plans/{testPlanId}member or abovedetaches a plan; the plan, its tests and its progress are untouched, and other milestones keep it204 also when it was not attached; 409 milestone_archived; 403 forbidden_role for a viewer
  • Plan progress and milestone readiness are derived on read in the database and the page; no endpoint returns them. The only progress the API exposes is the frozen copy written at close, which the plan list does not return.

Data: state-test-plan, state-milestone, flow-compose-test-and-plan. Features: FEAT-018, FEAT-019 (feature-test-design). Journey (e2e map): journey-plan-testing.

Group: run execution

Records what was executed, where, by whom and with what result. The run-state writes are the only ones that need run:execute: start (POST /runs), mark a step, finish with a verdict, abort with a reason, plus the evidence calls (group-evidence) and run submission (group-automated-runs). Reads (atc:read): one Run with its frozen chain, a project run report, a Test's run history, the workspace's active runs and the workspace-wide Run list.

  • Executor: a browser start is always recorded as human; a PAT may declare human, agent or ci (422 otherwise). The Run reads now carry executor_name (the token name for automated runs) and evidence_urls.
  • Two duplicate guards: the Idempotency-Key header (required, replays the stored answer) and the start_token body field (same Test and token within 24 hours returns the running Run with 200 instead of 201).
  • Only a running Run accepts marks, finish or abort (409 with reasons run_step_marking_closed, run_not_finishable, run_not_abortable). The finish verdict is the caller's choice, not computed, and the duration is derived from the Run timestamps (a caller-supplied duration is ignored). A missing Run on abort or finish is 404.
  • Marking a step: a cookie session re-marking is last-write-wins; a bearer caller re-reporting a step that already has a result gets 200 for an identical status, note and evidence (nothing changes, executed_at does not move) and 409 run_step_conflict for a different one. An optional Idempotency-Key header is honoured on the mark.
  • A Run left without activity for 4 hours is aborted by the database sweep (every 15 minutes); an agent or ci Run with no step report for 60 minutes is aborted by its own sweep (every 5 minutes) with a reason starting "Inactivity timeout", keeping the reported steps; a later mark gets 409.
  • GET /workspaces/{id}/runs (atc:read) lists every Run of the workspace newest first with step counts, keyset-paginated, filters travelling with the cursor; a foreign or lost-membership workspace answers the same empty 200, and a failing read answers 500, never an empty list. The project run report now splits totals into manual and automated; a Test's run history carries a flakiness summary. Comparing two Runs is group-run-compare.

Data: entity-run, flow-execute-run, state-run, state-run-step. Features: FEAT-020, FEAT-021, FEAT-032 (feature-execution, feature-insights). Journey: journey-execute-run.

Group: automated run submission and streamed results

Who calls it: a CI pipeline, a test runner or an AI agent that executes Tests outside Bunkai and wants the result on the same evidence trail as a manual Run. Two ways, both with a bearer token carrying run:execute.

  1. One call: POST /runs/submissions. The token must be bound to a workspace and its owner must hold the member role or higher there. Body: the Test, the environment by NAME (case-insensitive, never created), a verdict, a duration in whole seconds (up to 86,400; the Run finishes at submission time and starts that long before), one result per chain position 1..N (pass, fail or block, each reported once, up to 500) and up to 20 evidence links. The Run is created already finished, executor agent attributed to the token name, with run.started and run.finished audited.
  2. Streamed: start a Run with POST /runs (executor agent or ci), read each step id from the response, mark each step as it executes (any order, any subset), then finish or abort; steps never reported are recorded as skipped.
  • Answers of the submission: 201 created; 200 with replayed: true when the same idempotency_key and payload arrives again within 24 hours (the body key, not the header: this endpoint does not use the Idempotency-Key header); 409 for the same key with another payload; a rejected submission consumes no key.
  • Refusals: 403 token_required for a cookie session, 403 token_not_workspace_scoped for an unbound token, 403 for a viewer; 404 when the Test does not exist or belongs to another workspace; 422 validation_failed with reasons verdict_invalid, step_result_invalid, steps_incomplete (with missing_positions), steps_duplicate_position, verdict_inconsistent (passed needs every step to pass; failed needs at least one fail or block; contradictions are rejected, never corrected), duration_invalid, evidence_*, plus environment_invalid and no_executable_steps. Nothing is recorded on any refusal.
  • Streaming is retry-safe: an identical re-report of a step is 200 and changes nothing, a conflicting one is 409 run_step_conflict. A Run without a step report for 60 minutes is aborted automatically.

Endpoints involved: POST /runs/submissions, POST /runs, POST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark, POST /runs/{id}/finish, POST /runs/{id}/abort.

Data: flow-automated-run-submission, entity-run, state-run. Features: FEAT-045 (feature-execution). Journey (e2e map): journey-automate-via-api.

Group: image evidence on run steps and defects

Who calls it: the runner (a screenshot on a step), the bug form (images on a defect being filed) and automation that attaches proof. Images are stored in private Storage and never served from a public URL: bytes go straight to Storage with a signed upload URL, and reading is a 60-second signed redirect.

SurfaceWritesReads (atc:read, any member of the workspace, viewers included)
Run stepPOST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/attachments (init, run:execute, Idempotency-Key required, the Run must be running); POST …/{attachmentId}/commit (uploader only); DELETE …/{attachmentId} (uploader only, only while the Run runs, also cancels a pending upload)GET /runs/{id}/attachments (committed metadata of every step, oldest first, no path or URL); GET …/{attachmentId}/content (302 to a signed URL valid 60 seconds)
Defect being filedPOST /projects/{id}/bug-evidence (init, atc:write, member+, Idempotency-Key required); POST …/{attachmentId}/commit (uploader only); DELETE …/{attachmentId} (uploader only, never once a filing claimed it); then POST /bugs with evidence_attachment_ids and evidence_orderGET /bugs/{id}/evidence/{attachmentId}/content (302 to a signed URL valid 60 seconds)
  • Limits (inclusive): PNG, JPEG or WebP only, 10 MiB per file. Run step: 10 images and 50 MiB per step, 250 MiB per Run. Defect: one budget of 10 items (pasted links and images together) and 50 MiB per defect.
  • Init refusals: 413 file_too_large ("Images must be 10 MiB or smaller."), 415 unsupported_media_type ("Only PNG, JPEG or WebP images are accepted."), 422 validation_failed (reasons empty_file, invalid_filename) or attachment_limit_exceeded (reasons step_count, step_bytes, run_bytes, defect_count, defect_bytes), 409 run_not_open when the Run already closed, 503 storage_unavailable (safe to retry with the same key).
  • Commit checks what actually arrived: size from the object metadata and the type from its first 64 KiB. Not the declared image, empty or animated: 422 (reasons content_mismatch, empty_file, animated_image) and the upload is discarded; bytes not yet arrived: 409 upload_missing; window lapsed: 409 pending_expired. Committing twice is safe (200, same body). Nothing commits after the Run closed.
  • Visibility: an upload is invisible until committed (run step) or claimed by a filing (defect); evidence on a filed defect is fixed and cannot be removed (409 evidence_frozen). Missing, foreign-workspace, pending and deleted-workspace evidence all answer one identical 404; do not store or log the signed Location.
  • Cleanup: uploads never committed or never claimed are discarded after 3 hours and queued objects are deleted by the daily storage cleanup (auth-system-callers).

Endpoints involved: the nine listed above. Data: flow-attach-evidence, entity-evidence-attachment, state-evidence-attachment. Features: FEAT-044 (feature-execution), FEAT-022 (feature-defects). Journey (e2e map): journey-attach-evidence.

Group: run comparison

Who calls it: a tester or lead looking at a Run and asking what changed since the last time the same Test ran in the same environment. GET /runs/{id}/compare needs atc:read and is open to any active member, viewers included. It writes nothing.

  • The previous Run is the latest passed, failed or aborted Run of the same Test and environment that finished strictly before this Run started.
  • Steps are paired by ATC occurrence plus exact step text; a reworded step appears as Removed and Added, never as a change.
  • The answer carries a state: compared, no_previous, in_progress or unreliable. All four are HTTP 200 and only compared carries a verdict, counts and rows (groups: new failure, still failing, newly fixed, not comparable, added, removed, unchanged pass). A non-compared 200 means "no verdict", never "no new failures".
  • 404 is identical for a missing Run, a Run in another workspace and a non-member; 500 (fixed text) when the comparison could not be read.

Data: flow-compare-runs. Features: FEAT-046 (feature-execution). Journey (e2e map): journey-compare-runs.

Group: defects

Native defect tracking tied to the run step that exposed it. Writes (atc:write, member): file (201, Idempotency-Key required), assign or unassign, advance status one stage, correct title, severity, description and steps. Reads (atc:read): filtered list with aggregates, project list, single bug with origin and evidence, per-module heatmap, workspace open-bug counts, the workspace-wide defect list.

  • Filing from a failed step sends only run_step_id; the server derives project, module, run and ATC. Provenance from another project or run is 422.
  • Status is open → in_progress → resolved → closed, one stage at a time, never backward (422 with the next allowed stage in the message).
  • Assignee must be an active, non-viewer member (422). A non-member reading a bug gets 404, a viewer writing gets 403.
  • Bugs have no delete endpoint.
  • PATCH /bugs/{id} corrects exactly four fields, in any status including closed; status, assignee, evidence, Run, step, ATC and module never change and any other key is 422. It needs expected_version (the bug's content_version): a stale one is 409 conflict (details.reason = bug_changed) with the current defect in details.current; a save that changes nothing returns changed: false. An effective correction emits one bug.corrected event naming the changed fields.
  • Evidence: bug reads and the filing response carry evidence_attachments (id, position, filename, type, size). Images are uploaded before filing and claimed by it (group-evidence); filing with a bad attachment reference is 404 evidence_not_found (missing, foreign, pending, claimed and expired look the same) and a wrong evidence_order is 422.
  • GET /workspaces/{id}/bugs lists every defect across the workspace's projects, most severe first, keyset-paginated, with severity and status counts; defects of an archived module are neither listed nor counted; a foreign or lost-membership workspace answers the same empty 200 and a failing read answers 500, never an empty list.

Data: entity-bug, state-bug, flow-file-and-triage-bug. Features: FEAT-022, FEAT-023, FEAT-048 (feature-defects), FEAT-032 (feature-insights). Journey: journey-file-and-triage-bug.

Group: reports and search

What a lead decides on. All read-only, all atc:read, readable by viewers: project and workspace coverage (per criterion: uncovered, not run, executed; the workspace figure is one database function applying the project rules to every project, so the two can never disagree), one story's full traceability chain (criterion → ATC → Test → Run → Bug, with archived ATCs marked), recovery cycles per story, the workspace activity feed (a curated projection, never the raw audit payload; it now also names ATC archive, restore and update with affected Tests, module and milestone restores, defect corrections, member removals and Jira connection changes by site host only), cross-entity search (ATC, Test, Project, Module, Bug, Run) and recent projects for Home. A project the caller cannot see answers 404.

Data: flow-reports, entity-activity-log. Features: FEAT-024 to FEAT-028 (feature-insights). The workspace-wide Run and defect lists are described in group-runs and group-bugs. Journey: journey-review-quality (e2e map).

Group: notifications

The personal inbox and email preferences. All five operations are authenticated with no scope, because each caller only ever reads or marks their own rows: the workspace inbox (last 90 days), mark one or all read, read and update one preference cell. Notifications are not created through the API: database triggers write them when a Run closes or a bug is assigned or moves (see journey-execute-run, journey-file-and-triage-bug).

Data: entity-notification, flow-notifications. Features: FEAT-029, FEAT-030 (feature-notifications).

Group: team chat

A general channel per workspace where teammates talk and drop live links to ATCs, Tests and Runs. Who calls it: the chat panel; automation can use it too. All seven operations are authenticated with no scope: visibility is active membership of the workspace (RLS), so a PAT scope neither grants nor blocks chat. Workspace not found or caller not an active member: 404 on every call.

OperationWhat it doesRules a client hits
GET /workspaces/{id}/chat/messagesnewest limit messages; before_seq pages back; after_seq returns everything newer (reconnect catch-up, capped at 200)before_seq and after_seq are mutually exclusive; 422 on a bad limit, before_seq, after_seq or ids
POST …/chat/messagessends a message; optional mentions are recorded and each mentioned active member gets one notification in the same transactionmembers, admins and owners write; a viewer is 403 viewer_read_only; body trimmed, 1 to 4,000 characters (422 message_empty, message_too_long); 422 mentions_invalid
PATCH …/chat/messages/{messageId}edits one's own message; sets edited_atauthor only and within 15 minutes (403 not_author, edit_window_closed, viewer_read_only); 409 message_deleted; admins cannot edit others' messages
DELETE …/chat/messages/{messageId}replaces the message with a tombstone (body scrubbed, deleted_at set)the author at any time, admins and owners may moderate any message (403 not_allowed otherwise); idempotent; the tombstone never reveals who deleted it

GET …/chat/entities/searchfinds ATCs, Tests and Runs to insert as a reference; empty q lists the most recentmatches title, full id or ATC slug; at most 5 per type
  • Open browsers also receive Realtime inserts and updates on chat_messages; after a disconnect the client catches up by seq.
  • A mention notification reaches the member's inbox (group-notifications); on an edit only newly added members are notified.

Data: entity-chat, flow-team-chat. Features: FEAT-038 (feature-collaboration). Journey (e2e map): journey-team-chat.

Group: saved views

A person saves the filters they applied on one surface of a project under a name and restores them later. Who calls it: the filter bars of traceability, run history, bugs and the ATC workbench. Views are strictly personal: another member's view, another project's view and a nonexistent id all answer the same 404, and a list returns only the caller's own.

OperationCredentialWhat it doesRules a client hits
GET /projects/{id}/saved-views?view_kind=atc:readlists the caller's own views for one surface422 when view_kind is missing or unknown (traceability, run_history, bugs, workbench); a project the caller is not a member of returns an empty list
POST …/saved-viewsatc:writesaves the current filters under a name (201)at least one filter; name unique per member, project and surface (case-insensitive, trimmed, up to 80 characters) else 409 saved_view_name_taken; at most 25 views per surface and project, the 26th is 409 saved_view_limit_reached; state at most 4,096 bytes; 404 for a non-member
PATCH …/saved-views/{viewId}atc:writerenames and/or replaces the state; the surface cannot change409 name taken; 422 empty body or invalid state

Data: entity-saved-view, flow-saved-views. Features: FEAT-039 (feature-collaboration). Journey (e2e map): journey-use-saved-views.

Group: platform and system

  • GET /api/v1: version discovery; OPTIONS /api/v1 answers CORS preflight (not in the contract).
  • GET /api/v1/health: liveness only; it does not touch the database, so a green health check says nothing about Postgres.
  • GET /api/openapi: the contract file, rendered for people at /api/docs (bypass posture).
  • GET|POST /api/v1/admin/send-digest: the daily digest, cron secret only (auth-system-callers).
  • GET|POST /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup: the daily storage cleanup (03:00 UTC, production only), cron secret only; POST is the manual retry and the only way to run it on staging. It expires uploads never committed or claimed, deletes the Storage objects queued for removal and purges finished queue rows; the 200 body is the sweep counts. Not part of the public consumer surface (auth-system-callers, group-evidence).

Features: FEAT-030, FEAT-031 (feature-notifications, feature-public-pages).

Journey: build structure and author an anchored ATC

Purpose: turn a requirement into a reusable, traceable check. This is the value proposition: an ATC that escapes its story and criteria breaks every coverage and traceability report.

  1. Create a project in the workspace (atc:write, Idempotency-Key required); the plan's project limit may refuse it (422 project_limit_reached).
  2. Create a module, then a user story under it (Idempotency-Key required), then its criteria: the requirement must exist before anything can prove it.
  3. Create the ATC (Idempotency-Key required) with steps, assertions, the story and at least one of its criteria. The create RPC checks write role, criterion ownership and module subtree in one transaction and audits atc.created.
  4. Edit later with the version read: the database locks the row, compares versions and either replaces content and bumps the version (200, with the count of affected Tests) or answers 409 (an archived ATC answers 409 atc_archived instead). The edited ATC can be read back with GET /atcs/{id}.

Endpoints involved: POST /workspaces/{id}/projects, POST /projects/{id}/modules, POST /modules/{id}/user-stories, POST /user-stories/{id}/acceptance-criteria, POST /atcs, PATCH /atcs/{id}, GET /atcs/{id}.

Entities touched (business-data-context): entity-module, entity-user-story, entity-atc, flow-author-structure, flow-author-atc.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-authoring (FEAT-010 to FEAT-014), journey-build-project-structure, journey-author-atc.

Journey: execute a Test as a Run

Purpose: produce immutable execution evidence. A wrong verdict or a lost result defeats the product; this is also the path agents and CI use most.

  1. Compose a Test from ATCs (POST /tests, atc:write, Idempotency-Key required; a PAT names the workspace). Non-empty chain, same-workspace ATCs.
  2. Start a Run (POST /runs, run:execute) with the Test, an environment of the Test's project and optionally a start token and executor mode. The RPC copies the chain into a frozen snapshot with every step pending: later ATC edits never change this Run.
  3. Mark steps passed, failed or blocked with an optional note and evidence URL (an image can be attached to a step too, group-evidence). Each mark recomputes the run ATC verdict and is pushed live to browsers watching the Run. A bearer caller can retry a mark safely: an identical re-report is 200, a different one 409 run_step_conflict.
  4. Finish with the verdict the executor chooses, or abort with a 3 to 500 character reason. Pending steps become skipped; the starter is notified unless they closed it themselves in a browser. An agent or ci Run silent for 60 minutes is aborted by the database. Afterwards GET /runs/{id}/compare says what changed since the previous Run (group-run-compare); a finished Run can also be submitted in one call (group-automated-runs).

Endpoints involved: POST /tests, POST /runs, POST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark, POST /runs/{id}/finish, POST /runs/{id}/abort, GET /runs/{id}, GET /runs/{id}/compare.

Entities touched (business-data-context): entity-test, entity-run, flow-execute-run, state-run, state-run-step, flow-notifications.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-test-design (FEAT-016, FEAT-017), feature-execution (FEAT-020), journey-compose-test, journey-execute-test-run, journey-automate-via-api.

Journey: file and triage a bug

Purpose: turn a failed step into a tracked defect that keeps its origin, then move it to closure with the right people informed.

  1. Optionally upload screenshots first (group-evidence), then file the bug (POST /bugs, atc:write, Idempotency-Key required) with the failed run step, title (5 to 200 characters), severity P1 to P4 and up to 10 evidence items (links and images share one budget). Status starts open; bug.filed is audited.
  2. Assign it to an active non-viewer member; the new assignee is notified (the previous one is not).
  3. Advance the status one stage at a time; the reporter and assignee are notified, never the person who made the change.
  4. Fix typos or wording later with PATCH /bugs/{id} (title, severity, description, steps) using the content_version read; status and assignee are untouched.

Endpoints involved: POST /bugs, POST /bugs/{id}/assign, POST /bugs/{id}/status, PATCH /bugs/{id}, GET /bugs/{id}, GET /projects/{id}/bugs.

Entities touched (business-data-context): entity-bug, state-bug, flow-file-and-triage-bug, flow-notifications.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-defects (FEAT-022, FEAT-023), journey-file-and-triage-bug.

Journey: invite a teammate and join a workspace

Purpose: grow a team without sharing credentials, while keeping tenants apart. Cross-tenant leakage is the top security risk of a multi-tenant TMS.

  1. An admin or owner issues the invite (workspace:admin; a PAT must be bound to this workspace). The raw token is hashed at rest and returned once inside accept_url (201).
  2. The link travels outside Bunkai (chat, email written by the inviter).
  3. The invitee signs in and posts the token. Order of checks: token exists, workspace live (else 404, indistinguishable from a bad token), not revoked, accepted or expired (409 each), email matches (else 403), not already a member with an equal or higher role (409).
  4. One database call, bunkai_accept_workspace_invite, creates or upgrades the membership and stamps the invite accepted in one transaction (200 with workspace and role). It refuses with 409 inviter_not_authorized when the inviter was removed, demoted below the invited role or deleted since issuing the invite.

Endpoints involved: POST /workspaces/{id}/invites, POST /workspaces/{id}/invites/{inviteId}, DELETE /workspaces/{id}/invites/{inviteId}, POST /invites/accept.

Entities touched (business-data-context): entity-invite, state-invite, flow-invite-and-membership, entity-workspace.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-workspace (FEAT-006), journey-join-workspace-by-invite, cross-feature-active-workspace.

Journey: upgrade a workspace to Cloud

Purpose: revenue. The only flow where money changes hands, and the plan must change only on confirmed payment.

  1. The owner starts a checkout with a seat quantity (a workspace whose renewal is unpaid is refused: 422 plan_not_upgradable, reason payment_overdue). The owner check runs before the idempotency row is written, then a billing_checkout_sessions row is opened (one per workspace) before Stripe is called, so a double click cannot open two payments.
  2. The API creates the Stripe Checkout Session with that row id as reference and returns Stripe's hosted URL.
  3. The owner pays on Stripe. Cancelling on Stripe's page returns to the app, which calls the cancel endpoint.
  4. Stripe posts the signed event. Only a paid session upgrades the workspace to cloud and sets purchased seats; an expired or failed async payment releases the lock without a plan change. Later renewals are maintained in group-billing-maintenance.

Endpoints involved: GET /workspaces/{id}/billing, POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout, POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout/cancel, POST /billing/webhook.

Entities touched (business-data-context): flow-billing-upgrade, state-checkout-session, entity-workspace, integration-stripe.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-workspace (FEAT-007), journey-upgrade-to-cloud.

Journey: import user stories from Jira

Purpose: start from the requirements a team already has instead of retyping them. The only API flow whose work outlives the request.

  1. An owner or admin has connected the workspace to Jira beforehand (group-jira-connection); without a connection the call answers 409 jira_not_connected and leaves no job behind.
  2. A member posts the project and a JQL query (1 to 2,000 characters). A partial unique index allows one queued or running import per project (409 import_in_progress).
  3. The API answers 202 with the job id and starts the worker in the same request's after() slot.
  4. The worker pages Jira search 100 issues at a time with the workspace's own Jira credentials (no platform account and no environment fallback), converts each description, extracts criteria, picks or creates a module and upserts the story by Jira key.
  5. The client polls the job until completed (with created, updated and skipped counts and per-issue errors) or failed (a Jira authentication error fails the whole job as jira_unauthorized; a connection removed meanwhile as jira_not_connected).

Endpoints involved: POST /imports, GET /imports/{id}.

Entities touched (business-data-context): flow-jira-import, state-async-job, entity-user-story, integration-jira.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-authoring (FEAT-013), journey-build-project-structure.

Journey: delete and restore a workspace

Purpose: let an owner end a tenant safely. Blast radius is the whole team, and after 30 days it is irreversible.

  1. The owner calls DELETE /workspaces/{id} from a browser (a PAT gets 403; a non-owner 403; an already deleted workspace 404). Other members cannot veto.
  2. In one transaction the workspace is flagged deleted, its bound tokens and pending invites are revoked and a tombstone is written. The API answers 200.
  3. After the response, an after() task emails the restore link to the owner and every active member through Resend; a mail failure does not undo the deletion.
  4. From then on every route answers as if the workspace did not exist, for everyone. Within 30 days the owner can POST /workspaces/{id}/restore (409 not_deleted if it is not deleted, 409 restore_window_closed once the 30-day window has passed); revoked tokens and invites stay revoked.
  5. After 30 days the daily pg_cron purge deletes the workspace and everything that cascades from it; the tombstone survives.

Endpoints involved: DELETE /workspaces/{id}, POST /workspaces/{id}/restore.

Entities touched (business-data-context): flow-workspace-deletion, state-workspace, integration-resend.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-workspace (FEAT-009), journey-delete-and-restore-workspace.

Architecture behind the API

One Next.js application on Vercel serves both the UI and /api/v1 as serverless route handlers; there is no separate backend, queue or cache. Business rules live in Postgres functions (bunkai_* RPCs) and Row Level Security; handlers parse, authenticate, call one RPC or an RLS-checked query, and map errors. The system figure is at the top of this map (section overview).

ComponentRolePersistence / integrations touchedWhy it matters for QA
Middleware (middleware.ts)Refreshes the Supabase session cookie on every non-static request; redirects signed-out page visits to /loginSupabase Auth (getUser per request)Never blocks /api/*: an API test without credentials reaches the gateway and gets the envelope 401, not a redirect
Gateway (withApiHandler, lib/api/handler.ts)Request id, JSON access log, posture and scope checks, error envelopenone itselfEvery response carries x-request-id; quote it in bug reports. Any thrown non-API error becomes 500 internal_error
Principal resolution (lib/api/principal.ts, middleware/bearer.ts, user-jwt.ts)Cookie or PAT → one principal with an RLS-scoped clientaccess_tokens (service role), Supabase AuthCookie and PAT reach the same handler code, so one functional test per behaviour plus an auth-matrix test per posture is enough
Route handlers (app/api/v1/**, 157 handlers)Parse with zod (422 on invalid body), call the RPC, shape the responsePostgres via PostgRESTRequest validation is in zod; business validation is in the database (SQLSTATE mapped per domain, error-semantics)

A replay after the 24-hour row expired is a new request (the expired row is deleted with a compare-and-set). Route wiring is shared (lib/api/idempotent-create.ts)
Rate limiter (lib/auth/rate-limit.ts)Sliding-window counters per keyed digest of network source or account, fail closedrate_limit_hits via bunkai_rate_limit_consumeApplies to check-email, sign-in and code confirm only (auth-rate-limits); tests from one address share one budget

Service-role client (lib/supabase/admin.ts)Bypasses RLS for token lookup, token and invite secrets, invite acceptance, idempotency rows, rate-limit counters, Jira credentials (Vault), webhook, digest, storage cleanup, workerssecret tables, Vault, StorageHandlers using it must check authorisation in code; these are the places to probe for tenant leaks

Deployment shape: one Vercel project per environment URL; both Vercel crons (digest 08:00 UTC, storage cleanup 03:00 UTC) are registered from production only. Rate limiting: an app-level throttle on check-email, sign-in and code confirm (auth-rate-limits); sign-up, resend and magic link depend on Supabase Auth's own limits, which surface as 429. File evidence lives in a private Storage bucket reached only through signed URLs minted by the API.

Error semantics

Every error from a gateway-wrapped route is one envelope: { error: { code, message, details?, request_id } } with the same id in the x-request-id header. Clients branch on code and, for finer cases, on details.reason; the message is for people. The 4 bypass routes do not use it (the OAuth callback answers { code: "OAUTH_STATE_MISMATCH" } or redirects).

CodeHTTPWhat it means to the caller
bad_request400body is not JSON, a path id is malformed, a required header is missing (Stripe signature), an invalid cursor
idempotency_key_required / idempotency_key_invalid400send an Idempotency-Key of 8 to 128 word characters or dashes on the fourteen idempotent creates (architecture)
unauthorized401no or bad credential; for PATs always "Invalid token." whatever the cause
forbidden403wrong credential type (cookie-only), missing scope (missing_capability), wrong token binding, or role too low (not_a_member, owner-only actions)
not_found404missing, or in a workspace the caller cannot see (deliberately the same answer); also export not ready or expired
conflict409stale version, closed Run, duplicate active job, idempotency key reuse, invite already used, last owner leaving; finer cases in details.reason (atc_archived, milestone_archived, milestone_name_archived, milestone_plan_exists, test_plan_not_open, run_step_conflict, bug_changed, run_not_open, upload_missing, pending_expired, evidence_frozen, jira_not_connected, queue_confirmation_required, queue_count_mismatch, restore_window_closed, inviter_not_authorized, cannot_remove_self, sole_owner, saved_view_name_taken, saved_view_limit_reached, module restore reasons)
no_active_subscription, retry_not_available, invoice_pdf_unavailable409billing maintenance refusals: no paid subscription, no failed renewal or no new card yet (details.reason), invoice file not available right now (details.retryable)
slug_collision, checkout_in_progress409retry with a new request / wait for or cancel the open checkout
validation_failed422zod body validation (details = the issues) or a database rule (details.reason names it)
ac_outside_user_story, module_outside_project_subtree, chain_empty, chain_mismatch, chain_invalid, no_executable_steps, environment_invalid, test_outside_plan_project, plan_not_upgradable, seat_quantity_invalid, project_limit_reached, steps_position_invalid422named business rule violations a client can branch on without parsing text
payment_declined402the retry of a failed renewal was declined or needs a card action (details.reason card_declined or requires_action); nothing changed
file_too_large413an evidence image above 10 MiB
unsupported_media_type415evidence that is not PNG, JPEG or WebP
attachment_limit_exceeded422an evidence quota is full (details.reason step_count, step_bytes, run_bytes, defect_count, defect_bytes)
rate_limited429the app throttle (check-email, sign-in, code confirm: Retry-After and details.retry_after_seconds) or Supabase Auth's own limit on the sign-in family; also details.reason = check_in_progress when a Jira check by the same person is already running
internal_error500anything unmapped, including a database error a mapper does not know (its raw message is passed through)
upstream_error502Supabase Auth or Stripe failed, the rate-limit store could not answer (fail closed), or the webhook saw an unknown checkout session or customer
payment_processor_unavailable503Stripe unreachable or not configured (checkout and billing maintenance)
storage_unavailable503file storage unreachable on an evidence call; safe to retry with the same Idempotency-Key
method_not_allowed405declared in the envelope; no handler throws it in the snapshot

How database rules become HTTP answers

Business functions raise custom SQLSTATEs in the 45xxx range; each domain has one mapper (lib/atcs/errors.ts, lib/runs/errors.ts, lib/bugs/errors.ts, lib/tests/errors.ts, lib/test-plans/errors.ts, lib/environments/errors.ts, and response helpers for workspaces, modules, stories and notifications). Shared rules: 42501 (RLS or role refusal) → 403 not_a_member; P0002 → 404; unknown codes → 500.

DomainSQLSTATE → answer (selected)
ATC45020 → 422 ac_outside_user_story; 45021 → 422 module_outside_project_subtree; 45022 → 409 version_conflict + current_version; 45024 → 422 tags limit; 45025 → 409 atc_archived; 45026 / 45027 → 422 bulk_selection_invalid / bulk_change_invalid; 23505 → 409 slug_collision
Test45120 → 422 chain_empty; 45122 → 404 (ATC outside workspace); 45123 / 45124 → 422 chain mismatch / invalid; 45125 → 409 version conflict; 45126 → 422 tags
Run45200 → 422 executor mode; 45201 → 422 environment_invalid; 45202 → 422 no_executable_steps; 45204 / 45206 / 45212 → 409 run closed (abort / finish / mark); 45205 → 422 abort reason; 45207 → 422 verdict; 45213 → 422 step status; 45239 → 409 run_step_conflict; submission rules (45231 to 45238) → 409 key reuse or 422 reasons, 403 token rules
Bug45300 / 45305 / 45306 / 45307 → 422 provenance outside project or run; 45301 / 45302 / 45303 → 422 title, severity, evidence; 45310 / 45311 → 422 skipped / backward status; 45312 / 45313 → 422 assignee not member / viewer; 45314 → 409 bug_changed; 45315 → 404 evidence_not_found; 45316 → 422 evidence_order_invalid; evidence limit → 422 evidence_limit_exceeded with limit count or bytes
Test plan45600 to 45602 → 422 lengths; 45603 → 409 plan closed; 45604 → 422 test_outside_plan_project; 45605 → 422 nothing selected; 45606 → 404 Test not in plan. Close and reopen use a separate mapper that reuses 45603 to 45606 with other meanings: 45603 → 409 test_plan_not_open; 45604 → 422 verdict_required; 45605 → 422 verdict_invalid; 45606 → 403 close_forbidden; 22001 → 422 summary too long
Milestone45504 / 23505 → 409 milestone_plan_exists; 45505 → 422 plan_outside_project; 45506 → 422 milestone_plan_limit; 45507 → 409 milestone_archived; 45508 → 409 milestone_name_archived; 42501 → 403 forbidden_role
Workspacedelete or restore by a non-owner → 403; deleted or missing → 404; restore of a live workspace → 409 not_deleted; restore after 30 days → 409 restore_window_closed (45903); leave as only workspace or last owner → 409

Anti-enumeration: sign-in, magic link and token checks never reveal whether an account or token exists; POST /auth/check-email does, on purpose, and is now throttled per network source (auth-rate-limits). Non-disclosure is the rule of every new read: evidence, chat, saved views, invoices and run comparison answer a missing resource and a foreign one with the same 404.

Coherence check

  • Every journey touches entities present in the data map; no orphan entity was found. The new groups map to data flows flow-team-chat, flow-saved-views, flow-attach-evidence, flow-archive-and-restore, flow-compare-runs, flow-automated-run-submission, flow-billing-maintenance, flow-jira-connection-and-tracker.
  • Every journey maps to an e2e journey and feature. API-only paths without a UI feature: the headless sign-up, confirm and sign-in PAT minting (covered by journey-automate-via-api), the digest and storage-cleanup crons, the Stripe webhook, GET /me, POST /runs/submissions, the filtered GET /workspaces/{id}/projects that the Bunkai CLI uses.
  • Integrations listed by the e2e map that reach the API boundary (Supabase, Stripe, Resend, Jira, GitHub and Google OAuth, Vercel) all appear in integrations, and nothing extra.

Discovery gaps

  • No live API call was made (brief: read-only). Every status code, message and ordering here is read from code and the generated contract at origin/staging 4ccd8ede; behaviour on the running staging deployment was not observed. The first version of this map was read at 98ee1b4.
  • Contract versus code: the contract has 119 paths and 155 operations; the code has 121 route files. The two outside the contract are GET /api/openapi and POST /api/v1/billing/webhook; every contract path has a route file. The posture snapshot lists 160 handlers (155 contract operations, the webhook, and 4 bypass handlers). The posture scan itself was not re-run, so the 160 is the committed snapshot, not a fresh measurement.
  • Workspace-bound tokens: the binding is enforced by the 16 workspace:admin handlers (assertWorkspaceContext), by GET /workspaces/{id}/jira-connection and, in its own code, by POST /runs/submissions. Project- and resource-scoped routes (atc:read, atc:write, run state) rely on the owner's RLS only, so a token bound to workspace A appears able to act in workspace B where its owner is a member. Not verified live; whether that is intended is a product question.
  • The invite issue handler still writes the full accept URL, raw token included, to stdout (app/api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites/route.ts, console.log of the accept URL), so log readers can redeem a pending invite (same finding as the infra map NFR-SEC-010).
  • Headless sign-in and confirm mint a global, never-expiring PAT with atc:read, atc:write, run:execute unless the caller asks otherwise (pat_expires_in_days is optional); with about 8,900 non-revoked tokens in the shared database (data map, 2026-10-12 figure, not re-counted), test runs likely accumulate live credentials. How the QA repo's own bun run api:login sets expiry was not checked.
  • Unmapped database errors return 500 with the raw database message in error.message; how much schema detail that leaks in practice was not measured.
  • Bug writes need atc:write and reports need atc:read: there is no bug or report scope. Intended scope design or a gap: not confirmed. Chat has no scope at all (membership only); whether a read-only token should be able to post was not confirmed.
  • Rate limiter: the network source is read from x-vercel-forwarded-for or x-real-ip; with neither header (local runs, some proxies) all callers share one unknown bucket, so automated tests from one machine or one CI runner share the 10 per minute and 60 per hour budgets of check-email, sign-in and confirm, plus 10 per 15 minutes per account. Whether the staging deployment forwards a distinct source per runner was not verified. The QA repo's login budget is tracked in its own ADR (login budget under the sign-in throttle).
  • Bug sync to Jira: project tracker settings can be saved and queue defects as pending, but the data map found no worker or route that creates Jira issues; whether a later story ships the sender was not verified. Workspace Jira credentials sit in Supabase Vault; the QA role cannot read the connection table, so the number of connected workspaces and the presence of Vault secrets were not measured.
  • Plan progress and milestone readiness are derived in the database and the page; no endpoint returns them, so the API contract cannot assert them. How the frozen progress copy written at close is read back was not found.
  • Evidence: limits, the 3-hour window and the signed-URL lifetime were read from code and the contract, not exercised; Storage bucket policies were not inspected. How run start treats an archived ATC inside a Test chain was not verified.
  • Stripe: only the failed-renewal grace window, card replacement and retry are visible; no cancellation or downgrade path was found. Webhook endpoint registration, Stripe test mode, OAuth provider setup and Resend delivery per environment live in external dashboards and were not verified.
  • On staging neither cron is registered; a manual call to the digest or storage cleanup needs CRON_SECRET, whose presence on staging was not checked.
  • Contradiction with the data map: flow-compose-test-and-plan still says POST /tests has the idempotency key "supported"; the handler requires it (400 idempotency_key_required), as do 13 other creates.
  • Journey cap: 7 journeys traced (author an ATC, execute a Run, file and triage a bug, invite and join, upgrade to Cloud, Jira import, delete and restore a workspace).
